proposition.claim:
Let \(G=\operatorname{SL}(3,\mathbb R)\), \(\Gamma=\operatorname{SL}(3,\mathbb Z)\), and \(X=G/\Gamma\). A point \(g\Gamma\) represents the lattice \(\Lambda=g\mathbb Z^3\). The manuscript defines \[u(r)=I+rE_{23},\qquad
 a(t)=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{t/2},e^{-t/2}),\qquad
 a_0(\ell)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{\ell/3},e^{-\ell/6},e^{-\ell/6}).\] Its compact set is \[X_\varpi=\{g\Gamma:\|gv\|\geq\varpi
 \text{ for all }0\ne v\in\mathbb Z^3\text{ and all }0\ne v\in\wedge^2\mathbb Z^3\}.\] The exterior-square condition is essential: checking only lattice vectors would not test the theorem. For an oriented unimodular Euclidean three-dimensional lattice, the Hodge map identifies \(\wedge^2\Lambda\) isometrically with the dual lattice \(\Lambda^*=g^{-T}\mathbb Z^3\).

Equation reference: eq:main1, eq:main2. Theorem 1.3 on page 3 asserts that fixed positive \(\eta,t_0\) work for every \(t\geq t_0\) and every \(x_0\in X\), with one of the following alternatives: \[\begin{aligned}
 \left|\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}f(a(t)u(r)x_0)\,dr-\int_Xf\,d\mu_G\right|
 &\ll e^{-\eta t}\|f\|_S\quad\hbox{for every }f\in C_c^\infty(X),\\
 a_0(\ell)x_0&\notin X_{e^{-|\ell|/3}}
 \quad\hbox{for some }0.99t\leq|\ell|\leq1.01t.\end{aligned}\] The implicit constant is absolute under the convention on page 2. The Sobolev norm is fixed. Even allowing a finite constant depending on the single fixed lattice below would not repair the contradiction as \(t\to\infty\).

The notation \([L]\) means \([-L/2,L/2]\). Section 5 fixes \[\delta_1=\delta_2=10^{-5},\ d_0=10^{-6},\ C_1=10^7,\quad
 0<\theta<10^{-10},\quad \varepsilon_2=10^{-26}\theta,\quad N_1=10^5/\varepsilon_2,\] \[\varepsilon=e^{-10^5N_1},\quad\beta=e^{-\varepsilon^3t},\quad
 \delta_3=10^{-5}\theta\varepsilon,\quad \varepsilon_1=2\varepsilon_2.\] The iteration uses \(s_i=2^{-i}\delta_1t/2\) and \(d_i=d_0+i\varepsilon_2\). These constants, however extreme, are positive and fixed before \(t\) tends to infinity. No floating-point underflow is used to replace them by zero.

Two-sided a0 compactness alternative guarantees effective Haar equidistribution.
